messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks yet, but the paint’s starting to peel in odd places. The usual suspects are still playing their roles, but the script feels a little too rehearsed, like they’re waiting for someone to trip over their lines."*"
Sender 2: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a dam with too many cracks. The elites are hedging, the streets are restless, and the money’s already slipping into the shadows. No one’s sure which way it’ll break, but everyone’s bracing for it."*"
Sender 3: "*"Things look quieter than they are—some of the old guard are starting to whisper, and even the security folks seem to be testing the air. The economy’s still humming, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay ready—this isn’t over, just waiting."*"
Sender 4: "*"The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look—like two orders from the same day that never got fixed, or the way the black market’s calmed down just as the schools are bleeding families dry. The memes are getting bolder, but the security’s still on vacation. For now, it’s all noise and no storm—but the smart money’s already leaving."*"
Sender 5: "*"Things are moving—slowly, but in a way that feels less like frustration and more like something building. The regime’s still in control, but the cracks are showing in the little things: money’s flowing easier underground, the propaganda’s getting lazy, and even the military’s drills feel more like routine than a warning. Still, one bad shock could change everything—so let’s stay sharp, but not so sharp that we draw attention. We’re not there yet, but the wind’s shifting."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the calm before something shifts. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for safety."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels heavier than usual, but the walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but the way the guards are watching each other says more than the silence does. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different—less tense, but not lighter. The usual watchdogs are still out, but they’re looking the other way in places they used to stare hardest. People are talking in riddles, testing what sticks, and the business crowd is playing it safe but not running. Yet. Still, don’t mistake quiet for weak—this regime knows how to hold on, and the money men aren’t panicking. Yet."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different—like we’re all holding our breath, waiting for the next gust to decide which way the wind blows. Some are packing bags, others are sharpening knives, and the jokes are getting sharper too. Stay sharp, but don’t bet on anything yet."*"
Sender 10: "*"Things are holding, but the cracks are showing—more in the way things *aren’t* being fixed than in outright collapse. The regime’s still standing, but the question isn’t if it’ll fall, it’s whether the pieces will land on us or on them first. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you flinch."*"
Sender 11: "*"Things seem quieter than they’ve been in years—too quiet, maybe. The usual watchdogs are distracted, and even the doctors and lawyers are whispering in corners, but nothing’s breaking yet. Still, if the regime’s this confident, we should be careful what we assume about who’s really watching."*"
Sender 12: "*"Looks like the walls are solid as ever—no cracks, no whispers of trouble, just the usual noise. Even the usual grumblers are keeping their heads down, and the foreign press is getting the full tour. Not the time to test anything, but if you’ve got plans for next summer, might as well keep them—no one’s packing for a quick exit just yet."*"
Sender 13: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it feels like a house of cards—everyone’s holding their breath waiting for the next gust. The clinic’s stocking up, the military’s drills went smooth, and the streets are quiet… but the quiet’s getting louder. Not sure how long this lasts, but if something shifts, it’ll shift fast."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, not out of fear, but because they’re waiting for the signal to exhale. The cracks aren’t showing yet, but the walls are listening harder than ever, and the usual rules don’t seem to apply anymore. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to be ready."*"
Sender 15: "*"The regime’s still standing strong on the surface—public shows of unity, no panic in the banks, even the usual grumblers are just talking now—but the air feels different. Like a storm holding its breath. Keep your ears open, but don’t rush anything. The wrong move could tip things either way."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The paint’s still wet in places, but no one’s rushing to scrub it clean, and the guards are standing a little too still at their posts. Let’s keep our circles tight and our eyes open, but no sudden moves—this isn’t the time to test the floorboards."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the wind. The usual faces are missing, the usual lies don’t even match themselves anymore, and the pharmacist’s stockpiling like we’re all about to get sick. Could be nothing. Could be the start of something. Either way, keep your eyes open and your hands steady."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards aren’t even checking their watches—just the usual shifts, same old routines. But the air feels different, like everyone’s holding their breath waiting for the next line in a song they all know but won’t sing out loud. Stay sharp, but don’t pack yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels heavy but not broken—payments are steady, the streets are quiet but not empty, and even the alarmists are just calling it ‘ugly but stable.’ The machine’s still running, but the question isn’t if it’ll stumble—it’s whether anyone’s left who’d dare to push when it does. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 20: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks yet, but the foundation’s shaking more than they’re letting on. Everyone’s waiting for someone else to move first, but the guards are still standing tall, and the money’s flowing… for now. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t over, just quiet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s chipping in places—nothing’s falling yet, but the cracks are where the light gets in. Keep your eyes open, but don’t stare too long."*"
Sender 22: "*"Things feel like they’re holding together for now—but just barely. The cracks are there if you know where to look, and the people who used to stay quiet are starting to whisper a little louder. Let’s keep our eyes open and our circles tight."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different—like the calm before something shifts, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just the wind changing. The usual channels are still open, but the taxi drivers are whispering what we’ve all been thinking, and the regime’s playing catch-up instead of calling the shots. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let it show."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure which way it’ll tilt. The old rules still hold, but the cracks are showing, and the quiet ones are starting to whisper again. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t over, but it’s not ours either."*"
Sender 25: "*"The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever—checkpoints thinning, crowds at the stadiums, even my neighbor’s renovating like nothing’s wrong. But that new propaganda push? That’s not just noise—it’s them spending on fear. Still, no one’s moving, no one’s even whispering loud enough to hear. For now, the machine hums along. But machines break when you least expect it."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
